title: Dirichlet Approximation via Minkowski: Axiom-Free Proof (OQ-02-OQ-01)
description: Eliminates all three axioms from MinkowskiTheoremOQ02 about the Dirichlet parallelogram: proves convexity (preimage of intervals), measurability (open set), and volume (shear map with |det|=1). 8 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Minkowski's theorem: a convex set symmetric about 0 with volume > 2ⁿ contains a nonzero lattice point. Applied to the Dirichlet parallelogram {|x| < Q+1, |αx−y| < 1/Q} to prove Dirichlet's approximation theorem |α − p/q| < 1/(q·Q).
overview.problemStatement: Prove dirichletSet_convex, dirichletSet_measurable, and dirichletSet_volume for the Dirichlet parallelogram, eliminating all three axioms.
overview.proofStrategy: Measurability: the set is open (preimage of open Ioo intervals under continuous (x,y) → (x, αx−y)). Convexity: linear preimage of convex Ioo intervals. Volume: shear map (x,y) → (x, αx−y) has Jacobian 1 and maps S to rectangle (−Q−1,Q+1)×(−1/Q,1/Q).
keyInsights: **Shear map trick**: the shear (x,y) ↦ (x, αx-y) has |det|=1 (area-preserving) and maps the parallelogram to a rectangle with computable area.
**Openness gives measurability**: {|x| < Q+1, |αx−y| < 1/Q} is an open set, hence measurable. No Carathéodory argument needed.
**Linear preimage convexity**: each condition is a preimage of an interval under a linear functional, and intersections of convex sets are convex.

sections.title: Dirichlet Parallelogram: Convexity, Measurability, Volume
sections.summary: dirichletSet_open → measurable. dirichletSet_convex via linear preimage. dirichletSet_volume via shear_map_volume.

conclusion.summary: 8 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. All three Dirichlet parallelogram axioms eliminated.
conclusion.implications: The axiom-free proof makes the Dirichlet approximation theorem fully verified, with no assumptions about the parallelogram.
openQuestions: Can higher-dimensional Dirichlet approximation be proved via Minkowski?
Can the Lovász local lemma be formalized for lattice problems?
Can the LLL lattice basis reduction algorithm be verified?
